metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Windows: single-instance window reuse + Explorer multi-select as one playlist
tasks.description: Make Windows match the macOS open idiom (LaunchServices already gives the Mac one instance + one openURLs batch). Today each Explorer double-click/Open spawns a FULL new process (decode pool + resident VRAM ring each; settings.toml write races), and multi-select Open invokes one process per file (Explorer blocks >15 selections by default — MultipleInvokePromptMinimum — so the blast radius is capped at ~15 processes, but that is still bad). Plan: (a) accept multiple CLI path args -> classify_inputs (the Vec<PathBuf> -> LaunchInput::Files machinery already serves drag-drop/picker); (b) MultiSelectModel=Player on the ProgID (a REG_SZ value written by the existing per-user HKCU self-registration in default_app.rs — NOT an MSI component; WiX/MSI was retired when Velopack shipped, see archived task #51/#50) so a multi-select arrives as ONE invocation; (c) single-instance: named mutex, loser forwards its paths via WM_COPYDATA to the running instance (-> open_paths -> open_plan) and exits, winner comes to front (AllowSetForegroundWindow) — this also merges the multiple invocations Explorer emits when a huge selection overflows the ~32K command line. Compare-two-photos is NOT this task: thats #43 (or a future explicit File > New Window command, which the mutex design must not preclude — e.g. a --new-window flag bypass). MSIX/Store evaluation moved out to decisions.md (revisit only if monetizing). Windows machine required.
tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual: 'Set as default' opens the right Settings page; a second launch with single-instance adopts the new photo in the existing window. MSIX evaluation deferred.

Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Auto mode is an opt-in toggle: fine by construction on the Apple on-device backend, but a configured endpoint could be remote, and passive sends must be a deliberate choice. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. Custom prompt template = advanced, settings.toml-only in v1 ({filename}/{folder}/{datetime}/{location}/{camera} placeholders). Optional TTS via CoreEffect::Speak — AVSpeechSynthesizer / Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis, offline system voices, speech stops on navigation. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Privacy (ADR-018): never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk; the endpoint URL + toggles are the only persisted config. v1 scope: on-disk stills (archive entries punted like Delete). Interim HUD note: pb-hud font fallback helps the current paragraph renderer and non-Latin EXIF/text values, but task #54 makes Description/Ask a rich panel with selectable/copyable text; the HUD is not the final rich-text surface. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images). || WWDC26 CONFIRMED (2026-07-04, https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/): FM image input is NEW in the 2026 release (macOS 27) — on-device, ships with the OS, no download/setup; API is session.respond { PROMPT; Attachment(x) } where x = NSImage/CGImage/CIImage/CVPixelBuffer/file-URL, any size/aspect. VQA confirmed — the model answers ARBITRARY user questions about an image, not just captions (new subtask 9). WARNING: the 2M-first-time-downloads cap the owner saw is on PRIVATE CLOUD COMPUTE (the cloud escalation tier), NOT the free on-device model; and PCC is CLOUD, so per ADR-018 (never cloud by our hand) we request the ON-DEVICE model ONLY and never PCC — the cap does not constrain us. 3rd-party server models (Anthropic/Google) also plug into the FM framework, billed per-token — not our path. tasks.title: Vendor-patch wgpu-hal: presentsWithTransaction during window-mode transitions (flash-free resize, MTKView-grade)
tasks.description: Make the fullscreen-toggle / resize composite pixel-perfect on macOS. Today's mitigation (2026-07-04) is benign-not-atomic: layerContentsPlacement=.center + contentsGravity on the canvas view means the one racy composite ({new bounds, previous drawable} — wgpu presents out-of-band from the CA transaction that moves the bounds) shows UNSCALED stale content for <=1 frame instead of a stretch. The atomic fix is Apple's presentsWithTransaction (what MTKView flips on during live resize). wgpu-hal 22's Metal backend ALREADY implements the correct present branch (Surface.present_with_transaction pub field; present does commit -> wait_until_scheduled -> drawable.present(); the field's own doc comment cites resize-sensitive UI apps) — but wgpu 22 gives no safe way to SET it: Surface::as_hal hands out only a shared ref, there's no creation-time knob, and configure() re-asserts the flag onto the layer every resize (so flipping the CAMetalLayer property from Swift is useless). PLAN: (1) vendor wgpu-hal 22.0 with a ~20-line patch — interior-mutable flag (AtomicBool) + set_present_with_transaction(&self) — wired via [patch.crates-io] like the sevenz-rust2 precedent; (2) pb-render seam Renderer::set_present_with_transaction(bool) reaching the hal surface through Surface::as_hal; (3) flip it ON only around window-mode transitions (and optionally during live resize), OFF otherwise — presentsWithTransaction costs a main-thread waitUntilScheduled block per present, which MTKView itself only tolerates while resizing; the photo hot path (hold-to-fly) never resizes, keypress->photon untouched; (4) owner drives the upstream PR against wgpu trunk — NOTE trunk's Metal backend was rewritten on objc2 in 23+, so the trunk patch is the same concept but different code; a hal-level setter is the least-bikesheddable API shape. When the eventual egui/wgpu upgrade train moves off 22, the vendored patch drops (if merged) or re-rolls. Payoff is polish: the remaining <=1-frame unscaled reveal on F-toggles/live-resize becomes zero-artifact.

tasks.title: macOS window toolbar — nav + view/panel affordances (NSToolbar)
tasks.description: Owner idea (2026-07-05): a togglable toolbar for mouse-driven control — next/previous/random navigation buttons, toggles for the Inspector and folder-tree panels, and other frequently-used actions (rotate? delete? open?). This is a discoverability/mouse-affordance layer on top of the existing keyboard-driven core, not a new set of behaviors — every button should just fire an existing Action/PanelAction (Next/Previous/Random, ShowInspectorTab, ToggleTree, TogglePanels, etc.) through the same CoreEvent path a keypress uses today. Tension to resolve with the owner before implementation: CLAUDE.md's prime directive is a borderless, chrome-less window — an always-visible toolbar would contradict that, so 'togglable' likely means hidden by default and revealed on demand (a hotkey, and/or reveal-on-mouse-move-to-edge like fullscreen video players), never persistent chrome that eats into the fit-to-screen image area.

Shipped .app verified launch- and photo-load-clean.

tasks.title: Smoother hold-to-pan / hold-to-zoom — gentler acceleration curve
tasks.description: Owner feel note (2026-07-09): holding the pan/zoom keys accelerates too aggressively and doesn't feel smooth — want a slower, gentler ramp with smoother motion. The hold-to-view loop is AppCore::apply_view_holds (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:5642), driven by the tuning constants in crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs: zoom e-folding rate ramps ZOOM_MIN_RATE 0.5 -> ZOOM_MAX_RATE 2.5 over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS 0.7 (exp() applied multiplicatively about center); pan speed ramps PAN_MIN_SPEED 450 -> PAN_MAX_SPEED 3200 px/s over PAN_RAMP_SECS 0.7. Both are already time-based (frame-rate independent, dt-clamped to 0.1s) so 'smoother' here means the FEEL of the ramp, not a timing bug. Two levers: (a) TUNING — lower the max rate/speed and/or lengthen the ramp so it starts and stays gentler (e.g. PAN_MAX ~1800-2400, ZOOM_MAX ~1.5-2.0, RAMP ~1.0-1.2s), a one-file constant change; (b) CURVE SHAPE — the ramp is currently LINEAR in t (min + (max-min)*(t/ramp)); an ease-in (smoothstep / t^2) keeps fine control longer at the start before building speed, which reads as 'smoother'. Optional stretch: a short release ease-out / inertia so motion doesn't stop dead on key-up. Shared-core feel change (helps macOS + Linux too), surfaced while testing on Windows; keep it a measured, owner-in-the-loop tuning pass, not a blind edit.
tasks.details: Scope options, cheapest first: (1) Retune the six constants (ZOOM_MIN/MAX_RATE, ZOOM_RAMP_SECS, PAN_MIN/MAX_SPEED, PAN_RAMP_SECS) for a gentler start and lower top speed — pure constant edit in engine.rs, no logic change. (2) Swap the linear ramp for an ease-in in apply_view_holds: factor the shared 'min + (max-min) * shape(t/ramp)' into a small pure helper (e.g. ease_in(u)=u*u or smoothstep) so zoom and pan share one curve and it's unit-testable (assert monotonic, ease_in(0)=0, ease_in(1)=1, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Keep the multiplicative exp() zoom-about-center and the pan clamp untouched. (3) Optional inertia: on key release, decay the last velocity over ~150-250ms instead of zeroing zoom_started/pan_started immediately — bigger change, own subtask, only if the owner still wants more polish after (1)+(2). Note the scroll-wheel/trackpad steps (WHEEL_ZOOM_STEP, PIXEL_ZOOM_STEP, WHEEL_PAN_STEP, PINCH_GAIN) are a SEPARATE input path (AppCore::scroll, not apply_view_holds) — the owner's note is about held-key motion, so leave the gesture constants unless they ask. Prime directive: this is off the photo hot path (only runs while a pan/zoom key is held), so feel is free to change; still no per-frame heap alloc. Consider whether any of these should become settings (nav ramp/start/max are already configurable) vs hard-coded; default to constants unless the owner wants a knob.
tasks.testStrategy: Primarily owner feel-test on device (Windows first, then confirm macOS/Linux unchanged-for-the-better): hold each pan direction and zoom in/out, confirm the start is gentle enough for fine framing and the top speed is comfortable, not lurchy. If the ramp is refactored into a pure ease helper, unit-test the curve (endpoints, monotonicity, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Regression: apply_view_holds still returns changed=true only while keys are held (loop keeps polling) and pan stays clamped to image bounds; keypress->photon nav timing is untouched (this path is nav-independent).

tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): let the mouse pointer hide, as an OPTION, on every platform where possible. Half the plumbing already exists but nothing actually hides today: contract::CursorKind::Hidden is defined (crates/pb-app-core/src/contract.rs:80) and its doc even claims 'the viewer hides the cursor in the chrome-free hot path and restores it on movement' — but (1) NOTHING in the core emits SetCursor(Hidden) (hover_cursor at app_core_impl.rs:2678-2686 only emits Grab/Grabbing/Pointer/Default), (2) the winit shell STUBS it: cursor_icon maps Hidden -> CursorIcon::Default (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs:3361, with the note 'Hidden is unused on the SetCursor path'), so Windows/Linux never hide, and (3) only the macOS shell honors it (CoreModel.swift:1897 NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true)) — and even that is dead code since the core never sends it. So this is: wire a core auto-hide POLICY, make the winit shell truly hide, confirm macOS, and expose it as a setting. 'Where possible': winit uses Window::set_cursor_visible(false) (works on Windows + X11; on Wayland cursor visibility is compositor-mediated and may be a soft no-op — accept graceful degradation there).
tasks.details: Design: (a) POLICY in core — after N seconds with no CursorMoved (and no panel/dialog/menu open, and pointer not over a clickable affordance), emit CoreEffect::SetCursor(CursorKind::Hidden); any real pointer movement restores the resolved cursor (Default/Grab/etc via the existing hover_cursor path). Drive the timeout off the existing tick-deadline machinery (next_deadline / self.now) — do NOT add a spin; the app already sleeps when idle, so schedule a wake at the hide deadline. A natural stronger default: in the borderless Fullscreen 'speed mode' (WindowMode::Fullscreen) hide sooner or immediately-on-idle, since that mode is the chrome-free hot path the contract doc references. (b) WINIT SHELL — replace the Hidden->Default stub: on SetCursor(Hidden) call window.set_cursor_visible(false); on any other kind restore visibility + set the icon. Track visibility so we don't thrash set_cursor_visible every event. Windows + X11 honor it; Wayland may ignore — that's the 'where possible' caveat, log/accept. (c) macOS — the core now actually emits Hidden; verify setHiddenUntilMouseMoves gives the desired feel, or switch to explicit NSCursor.hide()/unhide() (persistent hide with our own restore-on-move) if the until-mouse-moves auto-restore fights the policy. (d) SETTING — add a serde-default bool (e.g. settings.hide_cursor_when_idle, maybe an idle-seconds too) and surface a toggle in BOTH shells (egui Settings General/Appearance tab via a pb-ui toggle_with_label + the SwiftUI SettingsView), defaulting per owner (likely ON in fullscreen, or a simple global ON/OFF). Privacy #2: cursor state is ephemeral runtime state; the only persisted bit is the toggle in settings.toml — no viewing trace. Keep the policy pure/testable in pb-app-core (feed it 'now' + last-move time + mode + overlay state, assert it emits Hidden after the timeout and restores on move) so it isn't a shell-only behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: unit-test the idle policy in pb-app-core — given last-move time, now, window mode, and whether an overlay/affordance is active, assert it decides Hidden after the timeout and Restore on movement, and never hides while a dialog/menu/hover-affordance is up. Manual per platform: Windows (winit) — leave the pointer still over a photo, confirm it vanishes after the timeout and reappears on the first move; confirm it does NOT hide while hovering the Cancel-scan chip or with a panel/menu open; confirm it hides sooner/at-idle in fullscreen speed mode. macOS — same feel via the SwiftUI shell. Linux — X11 hides; note Wayland behavior. Settings: toggling the option OFF disables all hiding on every platform; the setting round-trips through settings.toml (and the SwiftUI FFI) and nothing else is persisted.

tasks.title: Resolve LGPL static-link compliance (libheif/libde265) before public/commercial release
tasks.description: The Windows binary statically links libheif + libde265, both LGPL-3.0. LGPL requires that users can relink the application against a modified version of the library - a static link alone does not satisfy this. Flagged in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md during the task #76 license audit (dav1d itself is BSD-2 and fully handled by the notices file; Linux AppImage bundles shared .so files so it already complies). Not urgent while the app is private/free, but a MUST before any public or commercial release (Velopack commercial plan).
tasks.details: Options, roughly in order of practicality: (1) Ship libheif+libde265 as DLLs inside the Velopack package - Velopack handles loose DLLs next to the exe; LGPL is then satisfied by user-replaceability; needs a vcpkg dynamic triplet build (x64-windows + arm64-windows, dynamic CRT implications to check) and a build.rs link switch. (2) Offer relink materials (publish the app's object files or a static archive on request) - legally valid, operationally clunky. (3) Replace libheif/libde265 with a non-LGPL path (WIC-only HEIC would lose the measured ~4.9x parallel decode win; a BSD HEVC decoder does not realistically exist). (4) Counsel review if commercial licensing of libheif (strukturag offers commercial terms) turns out cheaper than the engineering. Also do a quick sweep of the rest of the dependency tree (cargo license) for any other copyleft surprises while at it.

tasks.title: CLI polish: clap, --help/--version, session-override flags, Windows console attach
tasks.description: Make PhotoBlaze a pleasant cross-platform CLI citizen for scripted launches. Today (main.rs:3406-3525): hand-rolled args, no --help/--version, unknown flags silently swallowed; release Windows builds are GUI-subsystem so nothing can print anyway. Decision (owner, 2026-07-11): use clap 4 (derive) - binary cost is a rounding error on this exe, parse time is launch-only, and it buys polished help/typo suggestions/value validation/completions for a low-usage feature. clap lives in pb-app ONLY (pb-app-core stays toml-only per NS0); the CLI parses into a plain LaunchOverrides struct the core consumes. Overrides NEVER persist to settings.toml (a scripted --dark --slideshow=5 launch must not rewrite the user's config).
tasks.details:
Order of operations in main(): (1) Velopack --veloapp-* intercept stays FIRST (update.rs:402); (2) Windows: AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) + rebind stdout/stderr BEFORE parsing (clap's help/errors are invisible without it; known cosmetic PowerShell prompt-interleave wart is acceptable); (3) clap parse; (4) launch. Register the hidden dev flags (--hud-gallery, --egui-shot, --settings-shot, --light, --tab, --welcome, --metrics) as hide=true so clap doesn't error on them. Parse-error fallback: no console attached (double-click / file association) -> existing Message dialog instead of a silent exit; console -> normal stderr + exit 2. Flag set (long + short where sensible), all mapping to existing state per the 2026-07-11 survey: --fullscreen/-f, --windowed/-w (exist); --recursive/-r, --no-recursive (exist); --info/--no-info (settings.show_image_info); --details (Panels.inspector, the Shift+I inspector); --folders (folder_tree_open); --slideshow[=SECS] (slideshow + interval); --scale <fit|fill|original> (scale_mode); --theme <light|dark|system> (appearance_mode); --mute (mute_live_audio); --shuffle (NEW small feature: start nav in the precomputed pb-core shuffle order - randomness today is per-keypress, not a mode); --version (build.rs build-id stamp, same string as About). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/bad path (with stderr message when console attached). Docs: README CLI section; optional clap_complete completions later. Estimate: 1-2 focused days; the AttachConsole shim is the only fiddly part.

RESOLVED DECISIONS (owner Q&A, 2026-07-11, branch feat/cli-clap): (a) STRICTNESS = Mixed - clamp an out-of-range --slideshow=SECS into [0.1s,60s] (matches the runtime slider's own clamp); --fullscreen + --windowed together = last-one-wins (no clap conflict error); a NONEXISTENT positional path still errors (exit 2, stderr when console). Unknown flags / bad enum values keep clap's own exit 2. (b) EXTRAS beyond #78's set: ADD --start-at <N|name> (open at the Nth photo, 1-based, or a matching filename, instead of the first; wins over --shuffle's random start; filename match applied once the deferred scan resolves). RESERVE --new-window as a parse-accepted no-op now, so the future single-instance task #1 has its documented bypass seam and clap won't reject it later. --sort <name|date|size|random> is DEFERRED (owner: cool idea but do it as a coherent app-wide sort-order feature first, not a CLI-only bolt-on); do NOT parse-accept it yet. (c) --shuffle MECHANICS (trivial - reuses existing last_nav-steers-slideshow design, app_core_impl.rs:2550-2553 + 1054): set last_nav = Nav::Random at launch so the slideshow AND hold-to-fly auto-advance in the precomputed random order; a DIRECTORY launch also does one random jump when the playlist resolves (start on a random photo); a SPECIFIC-FILE launch honors that file as the start (no random jump) but still sets last_nav=Random for a later slideshow. Manual Next/Prev (space/backspace) stay SEQUENTIAL and steer the slideshow back to sequential - the existing contract, matching the owner's ask (random slideshow advance + random dir-start, not random manual stepping). Flip to full mode later if wanted. (d) TDD: Cli->LaunchOverrides is a pure mapping unit-tested via Cli::try_parse_from([...]); --shuffle/--reverse/--start-at get pb-core/app-core tests. LaunchOverrides is a plain Option-field struct in pb-app-core (no clap dep); AppCore applies it, never persists. Docs: README CLI section + CHANGELOG (Added). Note: task ids were stringified by the adding commit; normalized #78 back to numeric per the tasks.json convention. (e) --reverse ADDED (owner, 2026-07-11): a direction seam over the four existing Nav variants, all routed through the launch last_nav (the slideshow + hold-to-fly already advance via last_nav, app_core_impl.rs:1054, and toggle_slideshow does NOT reset it :5102). Mapping: neither flag=Forward, --reverse=Backward, --shuffle=Random, --shuffle+--reverse=RandomPrev (reverse shuffle - already the Shift+Enter/RandomPrev action, keymap.rs:499). Directory start position: --shuffle=random photo, --reverse=LAST photo (runway to play backward), default=first; a specific-file launch always honors the file; --start-at wins over both. Runtime discoverability stays CLI-only here - the 'tap Left/Backspace during a running slideshow to reverse' steer already works emergently (manual nav steers the slideshow) and will just be documented; a dedicated runtime reverse toggle/menu item is a possible future micro-task. (f) ARCHITECTURE REVISION (owner, 2026-07-11): macOS CLI parity is now wanted 'now-ish' (owner finishes/tests on a real Mac later), so the clap parser is extracted into a NEW shared LIB crate `pb-cli` (depends on pb-app-core + clap) instead of living inside the pb-app BINARY - a binary crate can't be a dependency, and pb-app-core must stay clap-free (NS0). pb-app depends on pb-cli; later pb-mac-ffi depends on pb-cli too and exposes one FFI entry that feeds Swift's CommandLine.arguments through the SAME parser. pb-cli is FFI-ready by design: parse_from(args-iterator) -> Result<Cli, clap::Error> with NO process::exit (help/version/errors are clap::Error kinds each shell renders itself - which also serves the Windows AttachConsole + no-console Message-dialog fallback), and argv is always a parameter (never std::env inside the lib). The render-and-exit dev commands (--hud-gallery/--egui-shot/--settings-shot + --light/--tab/--welcome) STAY intercepted in pb-app before clap (as today), so the shared Cli holds only the real cross-platform flags (+ hidden --metrics). LaunchOverrides + launch_nav + apply_to_settings already landed in pb-app-core (green, 6 tests); Nav gained Debug.

Owner decision 2026-07-11: build the MIDDLE TIER directly (not the RAM-bounded short-clip version first): a forward-only streaming player - constant-memory discard ring + bounded-channel backpressure, real PTS pacing, audio-position-corrected A/V sync, coarse keyframe seeking - on top of the existing per-platform motion decoders (MF / AVFoundation / FFmpeg, which already stream from disk by path). Duration-independent by construction: a 2-hour feature film WORKS (flat memory, bounded sync drift, fast start) and is merely a lousy movie player by design (coarse seek only, no subtitles/scrub bar/resume - VLC keeps its job). MKV won't play on Windows/macOS (no OS demuxer) - graceful error; that self-selects toward camera content. Explicitly out of scope: subtitles, scrub-bar/timeline UI, audio-track selection, remember-position, hardware-decode/zero-copy (gated escalation).
tasks.details: PLAN (authoritative, rev2 2026-07-11 — Codex review verified + incorporated): .taskmaster/plans/79-video-playback-tier2.md. subtasks.title: Phase 3: reusable GPU presentation path (before long playback)
subtasks.description: Texture/bind-group + staging reuse for the animation present path; never wait on GPU completion on the event loop; measure alloc count + upload p95 before/after. Benefits GIF/APNG/WebP/avis; closes the #76 perf follow-up. DONE 2026-07-11: (1) ReuseSlot in pb-render::gpu - set_image (the animation/video present path) reuses texture + sampler + color uniform (UNIFORM|COPY_DST, rewritten in place) + bind group while geometry/format match; rebuild only on new-item/resize/SDR-HDR flip. ReuseOutcome::Reused keeps the renderer's existing bind group (wgpu 22 resources aren't Clone). (2) StagingUpload recycles staging buffers: map_async re-map after each copy, bounded pool (3), opportunistic - a miss allocates fresh, nothing ever waits on the GPU. Measured (present_path_churn, --ignored): 1080p p95 1.35ms -> 0.42ms (-69%), p50 -15%; 4K CPU-side memcpy-bound ~flat, but per-frame creations went 5 wgpu resources + 1 multi-MB staging alloc -> 0 in steady state. Tests: reuse-identity (global_id stable across frames, rebuilt on resize), staging recycle round-trip. Closes the #76 perf follow-up.

subtasks.title: Phase 6: seeking + contextual input
subtasks.description: Generation-safe latest-value seeks; keyframe + decode-forward landing (MF SetCurrentPosition / av_seek_frame+flush / AVAssetReader recreate); audio ack before resume; PAN-action contextual rewrite (+/-2s, Shift +/-15s, self-timed hold, custom-keymap tests); HUD position pill; paused/buffering/EOS/superseded cases. DONE 2026-07-11 (awaiting owner smoke): full 8-step seek spec. Producer: SeekTo{target,generation} on the merged channel ZEROES its credit balance (post-seek credits only - flush is race-free by channel order); seek = retire + recreate the reader positioned BEFORE first read (spike-locked; warm HEVC reposition blocks ~1s); decode-forward discards to the first frame >= target; a newer SeekTo supersedes every stage and a superseded landing never publishes; after EOS the producer PARKS (not exits) so replay/rewind works on the same session. Session: seek_to clamps inside duration (MF errors past EOS - 0xC00D36E5), bumps generation + flushes, freezes the clock AT the target (HUD), lands via Seeking->Buffering (new legal edge: Buffering->Seeking for held scrubs); resume-only-if-was-playing (paused seek presents ONE frame and stays paused); seek_by steps from the DESIRED target (scrubs the intent); audio ack gate ignores stale pre-seek samples until one lands within 1s of target; replay(P at Ended) = seek-to-0-resume. Input: horizontal pan actions contextually seek while a video plays and there is no horizontal overflow (pan wins zoomed); +/-2s, Shift +/-15s (default keymap adds Shift+Left/Right -> Pan*), self-timed 200ms repeat, OSD toast m:ss / m:ss. Audio: SeekVideoAudio effect -> SetPosition. Tests: 4 new session seek tests + 2 real-producer seek tests (landing pts>=target w/ new gen, supersede-never-flashes, replay-after-EOS). HUD position pill as a persistent element = phase 7 polish (OSD toast covers seek feedback).

MF's internal ConvertToContiguousBuffer copy); escalations reserved: IMF2DBuffer Lock2D (skip MF's copy), NV12 output + in-shader YUV (2.7x less data), hardware decode (ADR-012 gate). Linux/macOS parity split to subtask 9. subtasks.title: GPU-accelerated video decode (the 4K60 escalation)
subtasks.description: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-11 (end of session): GPU decode is NOT optional - software playback is only acceptable for the lowest-resolution videos; treat this as REQUIRED for the video feature to ship. tasks.title: macOS: play videos inside ZIP/7z archives (bytes-backed AVAsset parity)
tasks.description: Archive videos are indexed and typed on every platform (shipped with the Windows VideoInput::Bytes work, commit 2fb1317), but on macOS they show a placeholder poster and P toasts 'Videos inside archives can't play on macOS yet' — the native AVPlayer backend and av_poster.rs open media by URL, and an archive entry has no path. Bring macOS to parity by serving the entry's in-RAM bytes to AVFoundation via a custom AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate (fake scheme -> AVURLAsset), preserving the no-trace guarantee: never extract to disk. Windows is the reference: one Arc'd buffer feeds poster, playback, seeks, and audio. tasks.details: PLAN (authoritative, rev 2 2026-07-12 - Codex review verified + incorporated): .taskmaster/plans/83-thumbnails-panel.md. Rev 2 key changes (all four P0s verified against the code): (1) the decode pool needs a MULTI-CONSUMER contract first - set_targets today replaces the whole want-set keyed by bare item index, so thumb demand could cancel viewer prefetch; request identity becomes {item, epoch, purpose, fit-class, tier} with one merged priority order (DisplayCurrent > DisplayPreview > DisplayFull > Poster > ThumbVisible > ThumbWarm > ThumbRefine) + an occupancy guard (thumb jobs capped at max(1, workers-2), expensive fills only while parked) + displacement tests. (2) T0 derivation = POST-UPLOAD BUFFER HANDOFF (neither event-loop resize nor pre-Outcome worker resize): after drain_results uploads to the ring, the CPU buffer moves over a bounded 2-3-slot channel to a dedicated derive thread - zero clone, zero display latency; derive_thumbnail contract covers RGBA8+ColorTransform (downscale then bake the 3x3+TRC), Rgba16F (fp16 downscale + extended-Reinhard tone-map + sRGB encode), straight alpha, never Nv12 (video = posters); corpus A/B perf gate (capture on/off, decode-to-upload + keypress->photon p50/p95/p99 unchanged) is the acceptance criterion. (3) T1 is FORMAT-GATED - zune JPEG ignores allow_preview and always full-decodes; explicit matrix: embedded-preview capable (RAW/HEIC/PSD/WIC), JPEG via kamadak-exif IFD1 thumbnail (small new work), full-decode fallback (parked-only, capped, cancellable - placeholders while flying are CORRECT), native scaled-decode = future T2, video = posters. (4) Playlist::jump_to ALREADY EXISTS (the #43 compare flip) - expose it, don't rebuild it; cold-jump instant present needs a dedicated TRANSIENT PREVIEW SLOT (non-ring, never evicts the ring; <=1MiB upload ~20us on the click pump, full decode replaces via the normal preview->full swap). P1s: exact-byte budgets per owner (canonical 256MB ~ 256 worst-case square thumbs, in-flight = channel cap, per-shell visible+overscan texture caches, fallible alloc degrades to placeholder - not 'OOM impossible'); deck+request generations with clear-on-delete/rebuild + preserve-on-append (matches rebuild_playlist convention); eviction classes pinned-visible > overscan > warm > rest; shell bridge = dirty counter + <=1 notification/pump + snapshot struct + per-entry pull-once accessor; FollowState as a pure tested state machine (programmatic-scroll generation distinguishes user scrolls). Owner-settled UX unchanged from rev 1: Thumbnails name, Shift+T, playlist order always, no keyboard focus, fixed uniform cells, THUMB_EDGE=512, linear strip (no wraparound ghosts), smooth<=2 viewports else snap, type badges only, rotation at draw, find-ready item-list-view seam.

Port the same strategy: reuse the shared scoring (crate::video::poster_frame_score / POSTER_GOOD_SCORE / luma_stats_rgba8), add a head-walk then seek deeper (shallow-first offsets ~8/20/45/90s clamped to min(5min, 50%)) and pick the best-scoring frame. MF supports IMFSourceReader::SetCurrentPosition seeking; AVFoundation needs an AVAssetReader timeRange start offset added to the streaming reader (the harder one - the reader currently reads from the start).

subtasks.description: Give the Live-Photo streaming reader an AVAssetReader timeRange start offset so decode_video_poster can sample deeper into the clip, then reuse the shared best-frame selection. Covers MP4/MOV feature films on macOS.

tasks.title: Video ergonomics: space pauses a playing video + session-only resume positions
tasks.description: Solve the instinct to hit space to pause/play a video (space is the next-photo nav key, so today it skips away mid-watch). Contextual override like the arrows-become-seek precedent, not a new binding. Open design call: what space does on a PAUSED video (resume feels natural and stays symmetric; advance-to-next only when no video playback has begun, or on a stopped/ended clip). Applies to both the macOS native (AVPlayer) path and the Session backend; keep P working as-is.

subtasks.title: Space pauses (never advances) while a video is playing
subtasks.description: When the displayed item is a video and it is playing, space pauses it instead of advancing to the next item. Decide + document the paused-video behavior (recommend: space resumes, so space toggles like a media player once playback has begun; navigation resumes on a stopped/ended clip or a non-video item). Route through pb-app-core action dispatch so both shells inherit it; unit-test the contextual dispatch, including hold-to-fly (a held space advancing across items must not get stuck on a video).

subtasks.title: RAM-only per-session resume positions for videos
subtasks.description: Remember each video's last play position for the lifetime of the app session ONLY: a RAM map keyed by item, dropped in clear_session_state on Esc/quit like every other runtime cache, so the ADR-018 privacy guarantee holds (nothing persisted, no on-disk trace, and the no-trace integration test stays green). Returning to a longer video resumes from (slightly before) where you left off instead of restarting; near-start/near-end positions restart from 0 (thresholds TBD). Works on both backends: native = seek before play; Session = seek-after-open or an initial-position plumb-through.

tasks.title: HDR HEIC preview-first on Windows (WIC reorder)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #1 (Windows half). PQ/HLG HEICs bypass preview-first: wic.rs decode() returns the fp16 HDR full decode before the allow_preview thumbnail block, so HDR HEICs never get the fast SDR-thumbnail preview while scrolling. Fix: when allow_preview, try wic_decode_thumbnail FIRST (RGBA8, is_preview=true) regardless of HDR; only fall through to the is_hdr_transfer fp16 full when there is no thumbnail. The SDR8-preview -> fp16-full slot flip already works (upload_slot rebuilds the texture per call; drain_results upgrades a preview_resident item).
tasks.details: HDR capture is the iPhone default, so this is a growing class of photos. Verification harness gotchas: crates/pb-decode/examples/decode.rs hardcodes allow_preview=false (can't assert a preview) - use heic_bench or add a --preview mode reporting is_preview + PixelFormat. Confirm the test fixture actually has an nclx transfer 16/18 (an iPhone gain-map aux may not enter the PQ/HLG branch). Validate the WIC thumbnail's color: WIC exposes thumbnail retrieval and per-frame color contexts separately, so applying the primary image's colr to the thumbnail needs evidence, not assumption. Also make slot_bytes_estimate / VRAM planning fp16-aware if the sharp full-ring (prefetch_fulls, up to 8 workers) can leave the ring over budget after multiple 8 B/px upgrades (see #18.3).

tasks.title: Fill scale mode: cover-to-screen decode target (semantic Contain/Cover)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #2. decode_fit() returns None for ScaleMode::Fill, so a 24MP HEIC in Fill decodes/uploads at full res though only a screen-sized cover crop shows. Fix with a SEMANTIC decode target (Contain vs Cover) computed per-image after each decoder knows its oriented dimensions - NOT a single current-dims cover box in decode_fit (that mis-sizes neighbors: a portrait neighbor of a landscape current gets 2x-upscaled and it sticks once resident).
tasks.details: Owner decision (2026-07-14): use the semantic Contain/Cover target despite ~40 FitBox construction sites across 3 crates - a mechanical change, preferable to shipping a known sharpness regression. downscale_to_fit currently uses min() (contain); Cover uses max(sw/w, sh/h) clamped to no-upscale, computed against each image's own dims, so the box can stay image-independent (the screen box) and neighbors are correct too. AUDIT ALL 9 decode_fit() consumers (not just prefetch + slot_bytes_estimate): it also drives video scaling/budgeting, animation decoding, Live Photo streaming, and macOS archive posters. Benefit for HEIC is upload/VRAM/CPU-downscale (finalize applies the box after a full decode), not decode time.

tasks.title: macOS HEIC/HDR preview-first (Image I/O embedded-thumbnail decode)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #1 (macOS half). imageio.rs ImageIoDecoder::decode has NO thumbnail path and ignores allow_preview for ALL images (SDR and HDR) - so there is nothing to 'reorder' like the Windows WIC fix. Needs a real Image I/O embedded-thumbnail decode: CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex (embedded-only, so a missing thumbnail does NOT synthesize a full decode), with orientation + color-space handling, is_preview=true, and primary-dimension reporting; plus macOS compile + real-file preview/full-upgrade verification.
tasks.details: RATIONALE / IMPORTANCE (owner-requested, 2026-07-14): macOS HEIC preview-first is ENTIRELY ABSENT today - this is a NEW capability, not a regression fix. So Apple-Silicon users currently get no fast-scrub on HEIC/HDR libraries (every HEIC is a full decode on the scroll path). Importance: matters once the macOS build is a real shipping target; LOW URGENCY while Windows is the primary platform. Pairs with #95 (the Windows WIC reorder) as the cross-platform completion of finding #1.
